cap: High-risk HPV causes cancer only when infection persists and the viral DNA integrates, which breaks the E2 gene that normally restrains E6 and E7. E6 sends p53 for destruction, so damaged cells neither arrest in G1 nor die; E7 binds Rb and releases E2F, pushing cells into S phase. Because working Rb keeps p16 low, E7 activity makes p16 accumulate, and diffuse block p16 staining marks an HPV-driven high-grade lesion.
teach: Pair each oncoprotein with its target across the rows: E6 with p53 on top, E7 with Rb below. The green row is the practical payoff: pathologists use p16 staining as a stand-in for E7 activity when a biopsy sits on the border between CIN 1 and CIN 2, and low-risk types that stay episomal make warts rather than cancer.
